faq.q: What is the maturity period of Sovereign Gold Bonds?
faq.a: Sovereign Gold Bonds have a maturity period of eight years. However, investors have an option for premature encashment or redemption after the fifth year from the date of issue, typically on interest payment dates.

faq.q: How is the premature redemption price of SGBs determined?
faq.a: The premature redemption price is based on the simple average of the closing price of gold of 999 purity for the last three working days of the week preceding the date of redemption, as published by the IBJA.

faq.q: Are the capital gains from SGBs taxable?
faq.a: Capital gains on SGBs redeemed prematurely (after 5 years but before 8 years) are taxed as Long Term Capital Gains at 20% with indexation benefit. However, capital gains on redemption at maturity (after 8 years) are exempt from tax for individual investors.

faq.q: Is the interest received on SGBs taxable?
faq.a: Yes, the interest of 2.50% per annum paid semi-annually on SGBs is taxable. It is added to your 'Income from Other Sources' and taxed as per your applicable income tax slab.

faq.q: Can I sell my SGBs on the stock exchange?
faq.a: Yes, SGBs are listed on stock exchanges and can be traded. However, liquidity can sometimes be an issue, meaning it might be difficult to find a buyer at your desired price, especially for smaller denominations.

faq.q: What is the advantage of holding SGBs until maturity?
faq.a: The primary advantage of holding SGBs until their full 8-year maturity is that the capital gains realised at redemption are completely exempt from income tax for individual investors, making it a highly tax-efficient investment.
